title: Console request eligibility scoring, routing, and roadmap integration for enterprise reporting asks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers and internal CS/Support teams submit a variety of console/reporting asks (ad-hoc exports, tenant-level cost breakdowns, aggregated usage dashboards). Current triage is manual, inconsistent across reps, and lacks a repeatable way to estimate effort and SLA. Goal: create an eligibility scoring rubric and routing rules so requests are auto-classified into lanes (self-serve, product backlog, engineering commit, or enterprise service), and ensure prioritized items are reflected in the roadmap cadence and communicated to customers. This ticket scopes the product-side decisioning: intake form changes, scoring attributes, SLA lanes, roadmap mapping, and acceptance criteria. Engineering execution tickets and design mocks will be spawned from the decisions here.
acceptance_criteria: Define a 7-attribute eligibility scoring rubric (business impact, data sensitivity, recurrence, complexity, downstream customers, regulatory requirement, slack/time-to-need)
Update the console intake form to capture missing attributes (export frequency, data retention, PII sensitivity, desired SLA)
A routing matrix that maps score ranges to lanes: Self-serve (<10), Product Backlog (10-18), Eng Commit (19-24), Enterprise Service (>=25)
Documented playbook and communication templates for each lane (SLAs, expected delivery windows, and follow-ups)
Backlog tickets created for the top 3 enterprise asks identified during customer interviews and added to the Q2 roadmap with owners
steps: Run discovery interviews with top 8 enterprise customers and 6 CS/Support reps (complete)
Draft scoring attributes and initial weights (this ticket)
Design updated intake form and example flows (DES-41204)
Engineering to estimate high/medium/low work classes and confirm required infra changes (ENG-20412)
Pilot the scoring rubric on 15 historical requests to validate distribution and adjust thresholds
decisions: Use a numeric weighted score rather than categorical tags to give better gradation between 'product backlog' and 'eng commit' lanes
Default to manual review for any request flagged with 'regulatory requirement' or 'PII sensitivity' regardless of score
Expose the estimated lane and SLA to the customer upon form submission to improve transparency
Trade-off: adding more fields to the intake improves fidelity but increases friction; we'll progressively disclose advanced fields behind an 'enterprise details' toggle
progress_updates: 2026-02-25: Created ticket after synthesis of CS intake spreadsheet (Asha). Included initial hypothesis and target metrics: reduce manual triage time by 60% and reduce SLA misses for high-impact asks.

2026-03-07: Design sync — DES-41204 assigned to produce compact intake form with an 'advanced enterprise' section. Initial mock link added.

2026-03-09: Engineering sync — ENG-20412 to scope API and export schema changes; ENG-21780 to evaluate cost/compute impact for scheduled exports. Blocker: need canonical telemetry schema from infra team.
2026-03-12: Draft scoring rubric circulated to stakeholders; request to pilot on 15 backlog items approved. Moving to In Review for final sign-off by Head of Product and Solutions.
(Next) 2026-03-16: Pilot run and metric collection, then adjust thresholds and finalize routing matrix. Prepare roadmap PR for Q2 planning meeting.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-automating routing could surface low-priority work to engineering — Mitigation: conservative thresholds and mandatory manual review for high-risk flags
Risk: Intake friction reduces conversion of asks — Mitigation: progressive disclosure of enterprise fields and pre-filled answers for known customers
Risk: Data/PII handling creates compliance exposure — Mitigation: require PII checkbox and automatic escalation to Security/Compliance for any positive answer
